purpose: Teach: 単体/序盤/ワイルド/くわえ/不都合/幾度/当り/きまっ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが単体で旅をされたぞ
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to travel alone.
lines.style: Slow, nostalgic opening. Warm distraction in the voice—reaching back into memory. Slight pause after the opening address, letting the thought settle before continuing. Even pace, almost meditative.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、戦争の序盤を覚えていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear—you remember how your father used to tell you about those early war days?
lines.style: Soft, inviting tone. Gentle curiosity without pressure. The 'dear' lands with tenderness—affirming him as she asks. Patient pace, as if giving him room to remember.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはワイルドなお方だったぞ
lines.en: Your father was quite a wild one back then, you know.
lines.style: Slight chuckle beneath the wistfulness. A knowing look in the voice. Mild, appreciative tone—not disapproving. Settles on the word 'wild' with a glimmer of affection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、刀をくわえる写真があったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: I remember there was that photograph of him with a sword in his mouth, wasn't there, dear?
lines.style: Playful, gently teasing warmth. Lighter touch than before. The memory brings a smile into her voice. Slight rise toward the question, expecting his recognition.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、不都合なお話を聞かされたぞ
lines.en: People told me some rather difficult stories about those days.
lines.style: Quieter now. The wistfulness deepens—less nostalgic joy, more the weight of difficult knowledge. Measured pace. A pause before 'difficult,' as if he's choosing the word carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、幾度も村に貢献されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But he gave so much back to the village over the years, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Firm, grounding tone. Gentle correction—not dismissive of his sorrow, but steadying. The 'dear' is reassurance. She's offering him a different lens.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの直感が当りであったぞ, 本気で
lines.en: His instincts were right more often than not—I've seen it myself.
lines.style: Direct, with quiet conviction. The word 'itself' lands with finality—he knows this truth. Sincere, no softening. A man confirming what he's observed over a lifetime.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、結婚の日付をきまったとお喜びだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were so happy when he asked you to marry him on that particular day.
lines.style: Tender, intimate warmth. Almost a whisper. The memory of his joy pulls her voice softer, closer. Trailing slightly on the last phrase—savoring the moment.
